title: VOR Radials Without the Vertigo
hook: Which radial are you on? Wrong answer costs you the checkride.

scenes.narration: You're due EAST of the Baxter V O R, tracking toward it, when the examiner asks the classic: 'Which radial are you on?' Sixty-year-old tech, kid, and it still ends checkrides.
onScreenText: You're EAST of the station, inbound

scenes.narration: East of the station, flying west toward it. Which radial are you on — zero-nine-zero, or two-seven-zero? Commit.
Zero-nine-zero. Radials point FROM the station — spokes on a wheel. Why FROM? The station broadcasts bearings outward; your POSITION picks the spoke. Your heading has nothing to do with it.

Now the needle. Golden rule: set the course you're flying, and fly TOWARD the needle. Set it backwards — course two-seventy in the window while flying zero-nine-zero — and the needle lies to your face. Reverse sensing.
The H S I can't be fooled — its card rotates with your heading, so the picture always matches the windshield. Only instrument that never argues with me.
Eyes off the screen. Radials point which way — and what causes reverse sensing? Out loud.
FROM the station. Match the course to your heading. Fly toward the needle. And when the picture makes no sense — check what you twisted before you blame the airplane.
From the I L S lesson — standard minimums. Two numbers. Go.
A I M one dash one dash three. Old tech, current reg.

quiz.question: You're due east of the Baxter VOR, flying west toward it. Which radial are you on?
quiz.explanation: Radials radiate FROM the station — a position due east sits on the 090 radial regardless of which way you're pointed.

quiz.question: You get reverse sensing on a basic CDI when:
choices: The OBS course is roughly opposite your direction of flight
You're too close to the station
quiz.explanation: With the OBS set ~180° from your actual course, the needle deflects away from the course — fly-toward-the-needle becomes wrong.

quiz.question: Why can't a properly set HSI reverse-sense?
choices: The course arrow rotates with the compass card, keeping the picture oriented to your heading
It uses GPS instead of the VOR
quiz.explanation: The HSI overlays the course needle on a heading-slaved card, so the deflection is always shown relative to where you're actually pointed.
